meta.demo_note: Synthetic dataset generated by make_demo_data.py (seed 20261115). Shaped like real Garmin output, but fabricated — no real health data here.

block.context: Follows IRONMAN 70.3 Wisconsin (Sep 12, 2026). The aerobic engine is already built; this block converts it into run-specific volume and marathon-pace durability. Week 1 is re-entry, not training.

week.headline: Biggest aerobic week. Bank the volume, stay off the red line.

readiness.label: Recovery signals are strong — take the session as planned.

load.label: Load is in the productive range against your 4-week baseline.
load.method: Banister TRIMP from average HR where available, per-sport rate otherwise.

form.label: Deep in the work. Right for a peak week, not for a month.
form.method: EWMA, 42-day fitness / 7-day fatigue, seeded from the first 6 weeks of available load. Form is judged as a share of fitness so the bands don't depend on the load unit.

garmin.note: VO2 max and race predictions are Garmin's own models, stored each sync so they build a trend the API won't give you.

projection.note: Riegel extrapolation (exponent 1.06) from training runs of 5+ miles in the last 6 weeks. Riegel assumes a maximal effort, so a projection off training runs reads pessimistic — treat it as a floor, not a forecast.

projection.bracket_note: Garmin's model says 3:47:00; extrapolating your training runs says 3:53:08. Garmin models every run and reads optimistic; Riegel assumes a maximal effort it never got and reads pessimistic. The real number is somewhere in between.

race_day.pre_race: 2–2.5g/kg carbs, 3hrs out; nothing new on race morning
race_day.notes: You rehearsed 60–90g/hr on the 70.3 bike — running tolerates less than riding. Hold 60–75g/hr and practice it on every long run from Week 4.

carb_load.target: 8–10g carbs per kg bodyweight per day
carb_load.notes: Volume is already low in race week, so the extra carbs go to glycogen rather than fatigue.

fuel.note: Carbohydrate targets derived from the day's planned session. Calorie and macro *intake* is not tracked — Garmin carries no food log, so the dashboard reports targets rather than inventing consumption data.
